anyOf.description: It finished its answer.
The provider cut the answer off at its output token limit.
The model refused.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

AnswerStop.description:
Why the model stopped at its final answer. A daemon that does not know
why, as for a reason a newer SDK adds, sends `unknown`.

anyOf.description: As soon as the change is saved.
From the next turn of every loaded session.
From the next session the daemon opens.
When the daemon next starts.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

Applies.description: When a changed setting takes effect.

ApprovalAsk.description:
A tool asks to use a capability its session's permission mode does not
grant on its own.

reason.description: Why the policy asks, in its words.

anyOf.description: One of Rho's own tools.

A tool a host or integration provides, such as an MCP server's: a
different trust boundary from Rho's own.
Rho itself, as when it builds a prompt.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

May a tool use a capability? Answer [`InputAnswer::AllowOnce`],
[`InputAnswer::AllowForSession`], or [`InputAnswer::Deny`].

May the session leave plan mode to carry out its plan? Answer
[`InputAnswer::ApprovePlan`] or [`InputAnswer::KeepPlanning`].

Questions for the user. Answer [`InputAnswer::Answers`],
[`InputAnswer::Decline`], or [`InputAnswer::Dismiss`].
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

environment.description:
The asking client's environment, whose credential variables and
`RHO_CREDENTIAL_STORE` are that client's sessions' (#1779): a client whose
`RHO_CREDENTIAL_STORE` already chooses a store is refused as
[`crate::ErrorCode::EnvironmentOverride`], since the daemon's choice
would change nothing for it.
An empty one names no store and holds no credential, so the daemon's
own store is used.

AuthChooseStoreResponse.description:
Result of [`AUTH_CHOOSE_STORE`]: the daemon wrote and deleted a
temporary secret in the store, saved it as `behavior.credential_store`
in its config, and keeps credentials there from now on. Credentials
already saved stay where they are.

AuthKeyParams.description:
Params of [`AUTH_KEY`].

The key travels only over the daemon's socket, which is private to the
daemon's user (mode 0600) and refuses peers of another user, and the
daemon never logs it. `Debug` shows `[redacted]` in its place, so a
client that logs its requests does not log the key either.

auth.description:
The auth profile the key signs in to, such as `openai-api-key` or a
custom provider's `<name>-api-key`. It must take an API key.

environment.description:
The asking client's environment, whose credential variables and
`RHO_CREDENTIAL_STORE` are that client's sessions' (#1779): the key is saved to the
store it chooses, and refused as
[`crate::ErrorCode::EnvironmentOverride`] when one of its variables
already holds the profile's credential.
An empty one names no store and holds no credential, so the daemon's
own store is used.

key.description: The API key. Surrounding whitespace is ignored.

AuthKeyResponse.description:
Result of [`AUTH_KEY`]: the key is saved to the credential store the
daemon's config selects. Running sessions on the auth profile use it from
their next prompt; new sessions use it at once.

The daemon first asks the provider's models endpoint about the key and
refuses one the provider refuses with
[`crate::ErrorCode::KeyRefused`], saving nothing. A key the provider
cannot be asked about, because rho lists no models for it, the endpoint
did not answer, or the key may not list models, is saved unchecked.

unchecked.description:
Why the key was saved without the provider checking it. Absent when
the provider accepted it.

anyOf.description: With an API key, through [`AUTH_KEY`].

With the provider's interactive login, which the daemon runs and
relays to the client, through [`crate::methods::AUTH_LOGIN`].
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

AuthKind.description: How a client signs in to an auth profile. Protocol minors may add kinds.

environment.description:
The asking client's environment, whose credential variables and
`RHO_CREDENTIAL_STORE` are that client's sessions' (#1779): a profile one of its
variables holds a credential for is listed as signed in.
An empty one names no store and holds no credential, so the daemon's
own store is used.

AuthListResponse.description:
Result of [`AUTH_LIST`]: every auth profile that takes a credential, as
the TUI's `/login` picker and ACP's auth methods offer them, with the
custom providers of the daemon's config. Keyless profiles are left out.

AuthLoginCancelResponse.description:
Result of [`AUTH_LOGIN_CANCEL`]: the daemon is stopping the login, which
[`AUTH_LOGIN_FINISHED`] then reports `cancelled`. A login the provider
already approved still saves and ends `succeeded`. A login that already
ended, or no login, has the id: refused with
[`crate::ErrorCode::LoginNotFound`].

AuthLoginFinishedParams.description:
Params of the [`AUTH_LOGIN_FINISHED`] notification, the last one a login
sends.

auth.description:
The auth profile to sign in to, such as `openai-codex`. It must take
an interactive login ([`crate::AuthKind::Login`]); an API key goes
through [`crate::methods::AUTH_KEY`].

environment.description:
The asking client's environment, whose credential variables and
`RHO_CREDENTIAL_STORE` are that client's sessions' (#1779): the login's credential is
saved to the store it chooses, and the login refused as
[`crate::ErrorCode::EnvironmentOverride`] when one of its variables
already holds the profile's credential.
An empty one names no store and holds no credential, so the daemon's
own store is used.

flow.description:
How the user finishes a provider that offers both flows, `browser`
when absent. A provider with one flow ignores it.

AuthLoginResponse.description:
Result of [`AUTH_LOGIN`]: the login started. Its prompt and its end
follow as notifications on this connection, never before this response.
A second login to an auth profile with one under way, from any client,
is refused with [`crate::ErrorCode::LoginBusy`].

auth.description:
The auth profile to sign out of. Its provider's endpoint login, as
Ollama records one, is forgotten too.

environment.description:
The asking client's environment, whose credential variables and
`RHO_CREDENTIAL_STORE` are that client's sessions' (#1779): the credential is deleted
from the store it chooses, and the request refused as
[`crate::ErrorCode::EnvironmentOverride`] when one of its variables
holds the profile's credential.
An empty one names no store and holds no credential, so the daemon's
own store is used.

AuthLogoutResponse.description:
Result of [`AUTH_LOGOUT`]: the auth profile's saved credentials are
deleted, if it had any. Running sessions on the profile drop them from
their next prompt, which then fails with
[`crate::TurnErrorKind::Authentication`] until a key is saved again.

anyOf.description: It has a credential: saved, or in the daemon's environment.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

AuthStatus.description:
Whether the daemon's sessions can use an auth profile now. Protocol
minors may add values.

AuthSummary.description: One auth profile a client can sign in to.

auth.description:
The profile's id, which the auth methods take, such as
`openai-codex`.

label.description: What a picker shows for it, such as `ChatGPT Plus/Pro (Codex)`.

provider.description: The provider it signs in to, such as `openai`.

anyOf.description:
Every subagent run of every session the daemon hosts:
`behavior.agent_concurrency` in the daemon's config.

Claude-cli subagent runs, nested under [`Self::AgentConcurrency`]:
`RHO_CLAUDE_AGENT_CONCURRENCY` in the daemon's environment.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

Budget.description:
A concurrency budget jobs wait on, named for the setting that sizes it.
Protocol minors may add budgets.

anyOf.description: Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

CardTone.description:
How a [`SessionEvent::Card`] reads, so a client can color it or show a
card that reports an error as failed.

ChildThreads.description:
Who runs a session's child agents. The daemon reads it, so it has no
`Unknown`.

oneOf.description: The daemon runs them as subagents of the session.

The client's host runs them as its own threads, as T3 Code does: the
session's `agent` and `agents` tools delegate through the
`delegate_task`, `task_status`, and `task_cancel` tools of the
host's `t3-code` MCP server, which the setup's
[`SessionSetup::mcp_servers`] provides. While that server or one of
its tools is missing, every `agent` call fails rather than run the
child in the daemon.

value.description: What an answer sends when it picks this choice.

ClientCapability.description:
Something a connection declares it does, which the daemon then lets it
do. A method that needs a capability the connection did not declare is
refused with [`crate::ErrorCode::CapabilityRequired`]. The daemon reads
it, so it has no `Unknown`.

oneOf.description:
Answer a session's open requests, its approvals and questions, and
hold their timeouts: [`super::SESSION_ANSWER`] and
[`super::SESSION_HOLD`].

ClientEnvironment.description:
A client's environment variables, which a daemon session's children
see in place of the daemon's own (#1659): its tools' commands and
background processes (minus provider credentials), its MCP servers,
hooks, and OpenAPI sources, its CLI subagents and Claude Code advisor
(credentials included), and the workflow runs it starts. Values are
secrets: the daemon never logs or saves them.

Its `RHO_TRUST_PROJECT_*` variables are the session's project trust
when it opens or reopens the session: the daemon's own environment
grants none. A later prompt's do not change it.

Its credential variables, such as `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and its
`RHO_CREDENTIAL_STORE` are the session's too, from when it opens or
reopens until the daemon unloads it: the session's models sign in with
them, and a variable in the daemon's own environment never does (#1779).
Without the variables the session reads the daemon's own credential
store.

ClientInfo.description:
Who is connecting. Logged by the daemon; never used for authorization,
which goes by [`ClientRole`] and [`ClientCapability`].

ClientName.description:
A client's settings namespace, such as `tui`. It names the file the
daemon stores them in, so it is lowercase ASCII letters, digits, and
`-`, starting with a letter or digit, at most [`Self::MAX_LEN`] bytes.

ClientRole.description:
What a connection is for, which bounds the capabilities it may declare.
The daemon reads it, so it has no `Unknown`: a role this daemon does not
know is [`crate::ErrorCode::InvalidParams`].

A role is declared, not proven: the socket is private to the daemon's
user, and any process of that user may declare any role. It keeps a
well-behaved client to its part, so an agent's session-control client
cannot answer the approvals of the sessions it drives; it is not a
sandbox for a process that can open the socket itself.

oneOf.description:
A person's frontend, such as the terminal UI, `rho attach`, an ACP
host's `rho acp`, or a `rho` command. It may declare any capability.

An agent's session control: `rho mcp serve` and the `sessions` tool,
which start, prompt, and watch sessions for a model. It may not
declare [`ClientCapability::Answer`]: a turn that asks waits for a
person.

anyOf.description: Show the opening rows, for finished or replayed source.
Show the newest rows, for source the model is still generating.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

CodeWindow.description:
Which end of a [`ToolBody::Code`] stays visible when its card is
collapsed. The full body remains available on expansion.

anyOf.description: The prompt starts with `/<name>`, then its input.

`$<name>` anywhere in the prompt loads that skill before the turn's
first model request.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

CommandKind.description: How a prompt runs a command.

CompactionCounts.description:
A completed compaction's context before and after it, as rho counts
them: messages, and locally estimated tokens. A compaction that removed
nothing reports the same counts on both sides.

cost_usd_micros.description: What the compaction itself cost, when the session prices it.

CompactionId.description:
Identifies one context compaction; every [`SessionEvent::Compaction`]
with the same id reports on it.

trigger.description: What started it. Absent from a daemon that does not say.

anyOf.description: The turn was cancelled before the compaction finished.
It failed, or the run ended before it reported a result.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

CompactionStatus.description: Where a compaction is. Every status but `started` ends it.

anyOf.description:
A `/compact` prompt: the turn runs the compaction and no model
request, and its reply says again what the compaction did.

The session, within a model turn: the context reached its threshold,
or a request overflowed the model's window.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

errors.description: The whole error list, which replaces the last one.

values.description: Only the settings whose entries changed.

ConfigError.description: One problem in a settings file, by setting when it has one.

ConfigGetResponse.description:
Result of [`CONFIG_GET`]. From then on the connection gets
[`CONFIG_CHANGED`] for the namespace whenever a value or the error list
changes; reading the namespace again replaces that subscription.

errors.description:
What keeps the file from loading. While the list is not empty, the
values are the last ones that loaded, or the defaults.

anyOf.description: The user's global file.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

The agent's settings in `config.toml`, described by
[`CONFIG_SCHEMA`].
A client's own settings, described by its [`CONFIG_REGISTER`].
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

ConfigRegisterParams.description:
Params of [`CONFIG_REGISTER`]. Registering again replaces the client's
earlier schema; the daemon keeps it until it stops.

settings.description:
The client's settings. Each takes a [`SettingKind::Bool`],
[`SettingKind::Choice`], [`SettingKind::Integer`], or
[`SettingKind::Text`] value.

ConfigRevision.description:
Identifies one state of a namespace's values. Opaque: compare it only
for equality, and send back the one [`CONFIG_GET`] or
[`CONFIG_CHANGED`] gave.

ConfigSchema.description: Result of [`CONFIG_SCHEMA`]: every agent setting, in display order.

categories.description: The pages settings sit on, in display order.

file_only.description:
Structured tables `config.toml` holds that only a hand edit
changes, such as provider profiles.

ConfigSetParams.description:
Params of [`CONFIG_SET`]. Every change lands, or none does: a change the
daemon refuses leaves the file as it was.

changes.description:
Applied in order, so a setting another belongs to, such as an
internal agent's model before its reasoning, comes first.

revision.description:
The revision the changes were made against. A stale one is refused
with [`crate::ErrorCode::ConfigConflict`].

writer.description:
Who makes the changes. A revision stays good for its writer while
only the writer's own changes followed it, so a client that sends a
write before [`CONFIG_CHANGED`] for its last one arrives is not
refused for that change. A writer still sends each write only once
the last one's response came back: writes in flight together may
land in either order. Without a writer, only the current revision is
good.

revision.description: The namespace's revision with the changes.

ConfigWriter.description:
Names one client instance's settings writes, such as a terminal's, so
they never conflict with each other (see [`ConfigSetParams::writer`]).
Opaque: a client picks one unique to it, such as a random UUID, and
sends it with each write.

anyOf.description: A text resource embedded whole, such as a file the user attached.
A resource the user points at without its contents.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

ContentBlock.description: One piece of a prompt or a user message.

anyOf.description: The OS keyring: the Secret Service on Linux, the Keychain on macOS.
A private file under the daemon's rho home, not encrypted at rest.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

CredentialStoreKind.description:
A store the daemon can keep provider credentials in. Protocol minors may
add stores.

CredentialStoreStatus.description:
The credential store the daemon's environment and config select, which
every sign-in through the daemon writes.

unreachable.description:
Why the daemon cannot reach the store, absent when it can. The
daemon checks without writing, so a locked keyring counts as
reachable until a write is refused.

Cursor.description: Where a client is in a session's stream; send it back to resume.

credential_store.description:
The credential store the daemon keeps provider credentials in, what
chose it, and whether the daemon can reach it.

jobs.description:
Jobs with a turn in progress: [`crate::JobState::Running`] or
[`crate::JobState::WaitingForInput`].

socket.description: The socket the daemon listens on.

started_at.description: Unix time, in seconds, when the daemon started.

upgrade.description:
Set once the daemon's executable was replaced: the daemon re-executes
the new one in place as soon as nothing would be cut short.

DefaultAnswer.description: The answer the agent suggests for a question.

values.description:
What the answer would send: the value of each choice it names, or
the agent's own text where it names none.

anyOf.description: Pre-select it.
Only focus or mark it, so the user still picks it.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

DefaultStyle.description: How a client offers a question's suggested answer.

anyOf.description:
The client fell too far behind, the daemon unloaded the session, as
a delete that failed after it unloaded the session does, or the
session's conversation moved to another node of its tree; attach
again with the client's cursor.
The daemon is stopping.

The daemon is re-executing in place, for an upgrade or a restart, and
closes the connection next. Connect again, which waits until the
daemon answers, and attach with the client's cursor; the restarted
daemon answers with [`Replay::Reset`].
The session was deleted ([`super::SESSION_DELETE`]).

An observe ([`SESSION_OBSERVE`]) found the session unloaded: the
replay was the session as its file keeps it, and nothing follows.
Observe again to read it again.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

DetachReason.description: Why the daemon dropped an attachment.

DiffRow.description: One row of a compact diff body, with the line numbers for its gutter.

line.description:
Line number: the new file's for context and additions, the old file's
for removals. Absent for headings and for patch text without hunks.

stats.description:
Per-file `+N -M` counts on multi-file [`DiffRowKind::File`] section
headers. Structured so hosts style counts without parsing display text.

anyOf.description: Unchanged line kept for context.
File path heading in a multi-file diff.
Gap between hunks (`⋯`).
Non-content annotation (edit op locators, notices). Not a hunk gap.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

DiffRowKind.description: What a diff row represents, which decides its sign and color.

variable.description:
The variable in the asking client's environment that holds the auth
profile's credential, such as `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or the
`RHO_CREDENTIAL_STORE` that chooses the credential store, in the
client's environment or the daemon's own.

FastModeOptions.description:
Fast mode, which the current model has: faster responses at a higher
credit rate.

FileOnlyTable.description: A table of `config.toml` the protocol does not edit.

GrantAccess.description:
What a grant lets its holder do to sessions. Both sides read it, and it
is closed: an access a daemon does not know must fail, never widen.

oneOf.description: List, read, and wait for sessions.
Also start, prompt, steer, and cancel them.

GrantWorkspaces.description: The workspaces a grant reaches. Closed, as [`GrantAccess`] is.

oneOf.description: These directories and everything under them, as canonical paths.

capabilities.description:
What the connection does, each of which its role must allow; one it
does not is [`crate::ErrorCode::InvalidParams`], and the hello is
refused.

role.description: What the connection is for. It holds for the connection's life.

capabilities.description:
Optional features this daemon supports. Protocol minors add names
here from major 1 on; none is defined yet.

protocol.description:
The protocol the daemon speaks, which is compatible with the
client's.

IdempotencyKey.description:
A client's own name for one prompt, which makes sending it again
safe ([`super::SessionPromptParams::idempotency_key`]). Any
non-empty string the client will not reuse for another prompt of
the session, such as a UUID.

IdleWake.description:
What the daemon does when a session's background work (a workflow run
or a background process) finishes while none of its turns runs. The
daemon reads it, so it has no `Unknown`.

oneOf.description:
The daemon starts a turn that gives the model the result, as the
terminal UI does. A prompt's turn ends while the work it started
runs on. For a client that follows the session's events and shows a
turn it did not send. A session whose host runs its children
([`ChildThreads::Host`]) is woken through that host instead.

InputAnswer.description:
An answer to an input request. Each [`Ask`] lists the answers it takes;
any other is [`crate::ErrorCode::InvalidParams`].

oneOf.description: Approve this one use of the capability.
Approve this exact use for the rest of the session.
Refuse it; the tool learns `reason`, or that the user denied it.

Leave plan mode and carry out the plan in `mode`, one of the
request's `modes`. The model reads `feedback` with the approval.
Stay in plan mode. The model reads `feedback` as what to revise.

Answers keyed by question id: the values of the chosen choices, or
the user's own text where a question allows it.
The user declined to answer the questions.
The user dismissed the questions without choosing.

InputRequest.description: One thing a turn waits on a person for.

timeout.description:
When the daemon answers the request itself, if it will; absent once
the request is held.

tool_call.description: The tool call that asks, when a tool call does.

InputRequestId.description:
Identifies one input request among its session's, for as long as the
daemon has the session loaded.

InputTimeout.description:
An answer the daemon gives an input request at a deadline, unless a
client answers the request or holds it first. Only a question whose
agent offered fallback answers, in a session whose user set
`[questionnaire] timeout_seconds`, has one (#1660).

deadline_ms.description: Unix time, in milliseconds, when the daemon answers.

reason.description: Why the agent offered that answer.

anyOf.description: Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

JobId.description: A job's id. Opaque to clients: send back the string the daemon gave.

anyOf.description: The turns of a session the daemon hosts; see [`super::SESSION_NEW`].

One subagent run, started by the session or workflow job that is its
[`JobSummary::parent`].

One drive of a workflow run, started by the session job that is its
[`JobSummary::parent`]; the run's agent nodes are its child
[`JobKind::Subagent`] jobs.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

JobKind.description: What a job runs. Protocol minors may add kinds.

anyOf.description: Created; no turn has started.

The turn waits for an approval, a plan approval, or a question to be
answered with [`super::SESSION_ANSWER`]. Nothing is denied because no
client is attached; the wait ends with an answer, a cancel, or a
timeout the user configured ([`super::InputTimeout`]).
The turn failed; [`JobSummary::error`] says why.

The turn ran past the limit its prompt set and was cancelled;
[`crate::TurnOutcome::TimedOut`] says the limit.
The daemon stopped, or died, before the turn ended.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

JobState.description:
Where a job is. A session job's state is that of its current or last
turn; a subagent job's is that of its one run.
Protocol minors may add states.

created_at.description: Unix time, in seconds, when the job was created.

error.description: Why the job failed, when its state is [`JobState::Failed`].

grant.description:
What the turn under way, or the last one, of a
[`JobKind::Session`] job may do through session control: what the
request that started the turn asked for, held to `grant_limit`;
before the first turn, what the session opened with. Absent for a
turn without limits, as a person's own are, and for other jobs.

grant_limit.description:
The most `grant` may be, for a session that opened under a limit, as
one an agent starts through session control does: the grant it
opened with. The daemon holds every later grant to it, whoever
prompts the session: no shallower `depth`, no wider `access` or
`workspaces`. Absent for a session that opened without a limit, as
a person's own does.

parent.description: The job that started this one; `None` for a job a client started.

queue.description:
Where the job waits for capacity, when its state is
[`JobState::Queued`].

run.description:
The id of the subagent run a [`JobKind::Subagent`] job follows. For
a run a session started, it names the run's artifact directory
under the daemon's rho home.

session.description:
The Rho session the job writes; `None` for a subagent run on another
runtime (Claude, Cursor, Antigravity), which keeps its own.

updated_at.description: Unix time, in seconds, of the job's last state change.

workflow_run.description: The workflow run a [`JobKind::Workflow`] job drives.

workspace.description: The workspace the job runs in.

Location.description: A file a tool call touches, and the line when one applies.

LoginFlow.description:
How the user finishes a login whose provider offers both flows. The
daemon reads it, so it has no `Unknown`.

oneOf.description:
The provider's page redirects the browser to a callback the daemon
listens for on its machine's loopback, so the browser must run on
that machine.
The user enters a code on any device, as over SSH.

LoginId.description:
One login the daemon runs, unique across the daemon's life and
unguessable, so only the client that started it can name it.

anyOf.description:
The daemon saved the credential: once the provider approved the
login, or, for a provider that sends no confirmation, the credential
its prompt asked the user to approve.
The login failed; `message` says why, for a person.
A client cancelled it ([`AUTH_LOGIN_CANCEL`]).
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

LoginOutcome.description:
How a login ended. A login that saved a credential applies to every
session the daemon runs, as [`crate::methods::AUTH_KEY`] does: running
sessions use it from their next prompt, and each attached client gets
the sessions' new options.

A provider that sends no confirmation (Ollama Cloud's device key)
succeeds as soon as the daemon saved the login: its prompt's
`instruction` already told the user what to approve.

LoginPrompt.description:
What the user must do to finish a login. The daemon opens no browser:
the client opens [`Self::url_with_code`], else [`Self::url`], where it
can, and always shows the URL too.

`Debug` hides the device code, which signs in whoever enters it first.

instruction.description: What to do, in words, for a person.

url.description:
The page to open: the provider's sign-in page, or for a device-code
flow its verification page.

url_with_code.description:
The verification page with the code filled in, when the provider
gives one.

user_code.description: The code to enter on that page, for a device-code flow.

McpServer.description: An MCP server a client provides, by how the daemon reaches it.

oneOf.description: A process the daemon starts and talks to over its stdin and stdout.

args.description: The program's arguments, after its name.

env.description:
Variables the process gets on top of the session's environment,
by name.

name.description: The server's name, which its tools are listed under.

oneOf.description:
A server the daemon reaches over Streamable HTTP: HTTPS, or plain
HTTP only to this machine.

headers.description:
Headers every request to the server carries, such as its
`Authorization`, by name.

name.description: The server's name, which its tools are listed under.

MessageId.description:
Identifies one message in a session's event stream: chunks with the
same id extend one message.

ModelChoice.description: One model a session may switch to.

label.description:
A short name for pickers, unique within the list: the catalog name,
with the provider or model id added where two would read alike.

ModelOptions.description: The session's model and the models it may switch to.

auth.description:
The auth profile `current` runs on, which names how its use is
billed.

available.description: The user's favorites first, then the rest; always includes `current`.

ModelRef.description: A model, by its provider and the provider's model id.

anyOf.description: Rho's own model stack.
The Claude Code CLI, listed only where the daemon can run it.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

oneOf.description: Absent `model` lets the Claude Code CLI pick its own default.

NotificationCard.description:
Something that arrived for the reader: an agent message, a delegated-run
result, or a finished background process. Sources supply the data; the
renderer stays source-agnostic.

Fields added after the first saved journals read as their defaults when
absent, and are left out when they hold them.

body.description: Markdown shown in the card body.

output.description:
Verbatim text shown after `body`, such as a process's output tail.
It is never read as markdown; see [`NotificationCard::markdown_body`].

reference.description: Optional generic identity label displayed alongside routing information.

subtitle.description:
Replaces the sender/recipient routing line when routing is constant
for the card's source (for example, background processes).

anyOf.description: Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

NotificationDelivery.description: Whether the card's content waits for the recipient or has reached it.

anyOf.description: Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

NotificationPreview.description: How much of the body a collapsed card shows.

anyOf.description: Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

NotificationTone.description: How a notification card reads, which picks its accent color.

anyOf.description: Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

NotificationVisibility.description:
Whether the card belongs to the conversation or only to the activity
around it.

anyOf.description:
Run `program` with `args` in `cwd`. `shell_command` is the command
line, when the program is a shell running one.
Reach the network, at `url` when the tool names one.

Act on another agent session: `session` is the session the tool
acts on, absent for one it starts, `workspace` that session's
workspace, and `text` what it sends, absent for a cancel.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

Operation.description: What a capability would let a tool do.

anyOf.description: Under the session's workspace.
Under a directory the user added to the session, `root`.
Anywhere: outside every root the session knows.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

PathScope.description: Where a path an operation names lies.

PendingUpgrade.description: A replaced executable the daemon re-executes once it is idle.

version.description: The rho version the replacement reports.

waiting_for.description:
How many things the upgrade waits for: jobs in progress (queued,
running, or waiting for input), logins under way, and sessions with
work of their own, such as a background process.

anyOf.description: Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

PermissionMode.description: A session's permission mode, as `/permissions` names it.

PermissionModeOptions.description: The session's permission mode and the modes it may switch to.

PlanApprovalAsk.description: The session, in plan mode, asks to carry out its plan.

modes.description:
The permission modes the session may carry the plan out in; an
approval names one.

PlanEntry.description: One step of the agent's plan.

anyOf.description: Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

Presentation.description:
A transcript row has exactly one presentation.

Closed: each variant carries its card under its own key, which serde
cannot read into a unit `Unknown`, so a new variant is a protocol major.

oneOf.description: Facts-only receipt when collapsed; expansion reveals the full body.
Saved as `message`; the name predates non-agent notifications.

ProjectTrustMismatch.description:
The `data` of a [`crate::ErrorCode::ProjectTrustMismatch`] error: the
`RHO_TRUST_PROJECT_*` variables the session's trust and the prompting
client's differ in. At least one list has a name.

client_only.description:
The variables that grant trust the prompting client's environment
does and the session opened without.

session_only.description:
The variables that grant trust the session opened with and the
prompting client's environment does not, such as
`RHO_TRUST_PROJECT_HOOKS`.

ProtocolVersion.description:
A protocol version. Major 0 is the unstable protocol: every minor may
change anything. From major 1 on, minors add optional fields, methods,
and error codes, and only majors may change anything.

Question.description: One question, with the choices it offers.

allow_other.description: Whether an answer may give its own text instead of a choice.

default.description: The answer the agent suggests, if any.

header.description: A short label for the question, such as a tab title.

id.description: Names the question in an answer's `answers`.

required.description: Whether an answer must answer this question.

selection.description: How many choices an answer may pick.

QuestionAsk.description: Questions the agent asks the user, answered together.

QueuePlace.description:
Where a queued job waits: the budget it waits on, that budget's limit,
and its place in the budget's queue.

limit.description: How many runs the budget lets run at once.

position.description: 1 for the job that starts when the next slot frees.

anyOf.description: Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

ReasoningLevel.description: How much the model reasons on each turn.

ReasoningOptions.description: The session's reasoning level and the levels its model takes.

Replay.description:
What the events after a [`SessionAttachResponse`] start with.

Closed on purpose, unlike the event enums: a client cannot follow events
it does not know how to start from, so a new kind is a protocol major.

oneOf.description: The events after the client's cursor follow.

Discard what you have for this session, cursor included: its saved
transcript follows, then the turn in progress.

anyOf.description: A client answered it.
The turn no longer waits for it, as when the turn was cancelled.

Nobody answered or held it by its timeout's deadline, so the daemon
answered it with the timeout's answer.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

Resolution.description:
How an input request closed, as [`super::SessionEvent::InputResolved`]
tells every attached client.

RestartCost.description:
What restarting the daemon would cost, as of the moment the daemon
counted.

clients.description:
How many other clients are connected, which the restart disconnects.
They speak the daemon's protocol, so each needs updating or
restarting before it can use a newer daemon.

in_progress.description:
How many things the restart would interrupt: jobs in progress
(queued, running, or waiting for input), logins under way, and
sessions with work of their own, such as a background process.

RestartResponse.description:
Result of [`DAEMON_RESTART`]: the daemon has begun restarting. It detaches
every attached client as [`crate::DetachReason::Restarting`], finishes
in-flight responses, closes connections, records the turns it interrupts
as interrupted, and re-executes its executable as the same process. A
client that connects meanwhile waits until the restarted daemon answers.

anyOf.description: The provider limited the rate of requests.
Another failure that may pass, such as a server error.
The provider's response was malformed.

The request overflowed the model's context; the turn compacts it
first.

One request failed and the provider sends it again; no response was
discarded.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

RetryReason.description: Why a turn asks the provider again ([`SessionEvent::ProviderRetry`]).

SecretMap.description:
Values by name that may be secrets, such as an MCP server's environment
variables and headers. Its `Debug` shows only the names, so the daemon
never logs a value.

anyOf.description: Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

Selection.description: How many choices a question's answer may pick.

Seq.description:
Position in a stream: the number of live events sent before and
including this one, from 1. `Seq(0)` is not a position: a reset's
transcript events carry it (see [`super::SessionEventParams::seq`]), and
a cursor at 0 always resets.

answer.description: One of the answers the request's [`Ask`] lists.

SessionAnswerResponse.description:
Result of [`SESSION_ANSWER`]: the answer won, and the daemon handed it
to the turn. An answer that lost, to another client's or to the turn
withdrawing the request, is [`crate::ErrorCode::InputNotOpen`]. A turn
that stops waiting at the same moment, because it was cancelled or the
tool that asked gave up, ignores an answer that won.

after.description:
The last event this client has, to resume after it. Absent, from
another stream, or older than the daemon keeps: [`Replay::Reset`].

environment.description:
The environment the session opens with if this attach reopens it
(#1661): its processes run with it until a prompt brings another.
A session the daemon has loaded keeps its own.

setup.description:
The client's choices for the session if this attach reopens it. A
session the daemon has loaded keeps its own, and one a prompt
reopened has none.

SessionAttachResponse.description:
Result of [`SESSION_ATTACH`] and [`SESSION_OBSERVE`]. The session's
events then arrive as [`SESSION_EVENT`] notifications, never before this
response. Attaching or observing again on the same connection replaces
the earlier attachment.

inputs.description:
The input requests open when the attachment began, oldest first:
what a client may answer even when the replay no longer holds the
events that opened them (#1660). The replay may repeat some; an
input request's id names it.

options.description:
The session's options when the attachment began; a later
[`super::SessionEvent::OptionsChanged`] replaces them.

replay_events.description:
How many events the replay holds: the first this many
[`SESSION_EVENT`] notifications after this response replay what the
client missed, and the rest are live (#1669). A reset replays the
last turn's [`super::SessionEvent::TurnEnded`] until the next turn
saves, under that turn's id.

state.description:
The session's job state when the attachment began, which the replay
ends in.

stream.description: The stream the events belong to; a cursor names it to resume.

title.description:
The session's title when the attachment began; absent until it has
one. Saved transcripts hold no [`super::SessionEvent::TitleChanged`],
so a reset may not replay the one that set it (#1670).

turn.description:
The turn `state` is of: the one under way, or the last one, whose
end a reset's replay holds as the [`super::SessionEvent::TurnEnded`]
carrying this id. Absent only while the session has run no turn.

workspace.description:
The directory the session works in: the one it was saved in, for a
session the daemon reopened (#1661).

SessionCancelResponse.description:
Result of [`SESSION_CANCEL`]: the turn in progress, if any, has been
asked to stop. The turn saves what it did and ends
[`crate::JobState::Cancelled`], or [`crate::JobState::Interrupted`] when
the daemon is stopping; one already past its
[`SessionPromptParams::timeout_ms`] ends [`crate::JobState::TimedOut`].
A cancel that arrives before a prompted turn begins still cancels it,
and that prompt answers [`crate::ErrorCode::TurnEnded`].

SessionChange.description:
One change to a loaded session, applied between its turns: a setting, or
an edit to its context or to where its conversation continues from. A setting's value must be one the session's
[`SessionOptions`] offers; any other is [`crate::ErrorCode::InvalidParams`].

oneOf.description:
Switch to `model`, one of [`ModelOptions::available`]. The session
keeps its reasoning level, or refuses a model that cannot.

auth.description:
The auth profile to run `model` on, as `--auth` names one: a
profile `model`'s provider takes. When absent, the session keeps
its auth if the provider takes it, else picks one that has
credentials.

oneOf.description: Spend `level`, one of [`ReasoningOptions::available`], on later turns.

Turn fast mode on or off. Turning it on needs a model that has it
([`SessionOptions::fast_mode`] present); off always applies.
Gate later turns' tool calls with `mode`.
Control the loaded session's goal without waiting for its turn.

Add `text` to what the model reads from its next turn on, without a
turn of its own, and save it with the session as a user row that
reads `display`. Clients attached now see no event for it: the one
that sent it shows its own notice, and a later reset replays the
row. An empty `text` is [`crate::ErrorCode::InvalidParams`].

Read the workspace's agent definitions again and tell the model, from
its next turn on, which agents it can now delegate to. A client sends
it after it wrote or removed a definition. Clients see a
[`super::SessionEvent::Notice`] when the model had to be told.

Let the session's tools reach the directory at `path`, absolute, and
tell the model so from its next turn on, with a saved row. A path
that is not a directory, or one the session already reaches, is
[`crate::ErrorCode::InvalidParams`].

Read the model lists again: a client sends it after it refreshed
the lists the daemon shares on disk. Every loaded session's options
follow.

Continue the conversation from `node`, a node of the session's saved
tree, as it stood there: later turns branch from it, and the nodes
after it stay in the tree. The daemon then detaches every attached
client as [`super::DetachReason::Lagged`]; attaching again replays
the conversation up to `node`. A node the tree does not hold, or a
session that has saved nothing, is
[`crate::ErrorCode::InvalidParams`].

Put back the files the turn of workspace checkpoint `checkpoint`
changed, as far as they still hold what that turn left, and, when
every one was put back, continue the conversation from before that
turn, as [`Self::SelectNode`] does. Clients see what became of each
file as a [`super::SessionEvent::Notice`]. A checkpoint the session
does not have, a session in plan mode, or one with nothing saved is
[`crate::ErrorCode::InvalidParams`].

SessionCommand.description: One command a prompt may run.

input_hint.description:
What to type after the name, such as `<query>` or `[instructions]`;
absent for a command that takes nothing.

name.description:
The command's name, without the `/` or `$` its [`CommandKind`] puts
before it: `init`, `prompt:review`, `mcp:docs:search`, `pdf`.

change.description: One change per request, so an error names the change it refuses.

SessionConfigureResponse.description:
Result of [`SESSION_CONFIGURE`], once the change applied, after the turn
under way, if any, ended: the change applies from the next turn, and
these are the session's options with it. Every attached client also
receives them as [`super::SessionEvent::OptionsChanged`] when they
changed.

anyOf.description: Start a session with a first prompt.
Start a session's next turn.
Give a running turn input for its next model request.
Cancel the turn in progress.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

SessionControlAction.description: What an [`Operation::ControlSession`] does to the session.

unless_attached.description:
Refuse a session a client is attached to, as
[`crate::ErrorCode::SessionInUse`], rather than detach its clients:
for a client that deletes sessions it is not showing and cannot
tell which of them another client has open.

SessionDeleteResponse.description:
Result of [`SESSION_DELETE`]: the session's files are gone, with those
of the sessions it started, such as its subagents', and the daemon has
unloaded it, detaching its clients as
[`super::DetachReason::Deleted`]. Its job stays in [`super::JOB_LIST`].

A session whose turn is under way, a settings change waiting or
applying, background work running, such as a subagent, or a run it started not yet
finished is refused as [`crate::ErrorCode::SessionBusy`]; one another
process has open, or one a session it started is open in, as
[`crate::ErrorCode::SessionInUse`]. Either refusal leaves a loaded
session loaded. A session the daemon loaded but that has saved nothing
yet is unloaded all the same. An id the daemon has not loaded and nothing
is saved under is [`crate::ErrorCode::SessionNotFound`].

SessionDetachResponse.description:
Result of [`SESSION_DETACH`]: no events of the session follow. Detaching
a session this connection has not attached also succeeds.

SessionDetachedParams.description:
Params of the [`SESSION_DETACHED`] notification. No events of the
session follow; attach again, with the client's cursor, to resume.

anyOf.description:
The session's job changed state: a turn started (`running`), waits
for input, or ended. An ended turn's [`Self::TurnEnded`] comes first.

turn.description:
The turn the state is of: the one under way, or the one that
ended. Absent only while the session has run no turn.

anyOf.description: A user message, whole.

steer.description:
Present when the message is a steer that just applied: it crossed
into the conversation for the turn's next model request, under
the id [`super::SESSION_STEER`] answered with. Replayed history
carries none.

anyOf.description: More of the agent's reply.
More of the agent's reasoning.

Opens or updates a tool call; absent fields are unchanged. Boxed:
it is the largest event by far.
The agent's plan, replacing any earlier one.
How full the model's context is, and what the session has cost.

cost_usd_micros.description:
The session's whole spend so far in millionths of a US dollar,
so it stays exact, turns before a daemon restart included.
Absent while no request has a price, as when every request ran
on a local model (#1670).

anyOf.description:
The session has a new title, as when the daemon named it after its
first turn (#1670) or a client renamed it
([`super::SESSION_RENAME`]).

A context compaction began or ended. Each one starts
[`CompactionStatus::Started`] and ends with exactly one other
status, under the same `id` (#1670).

The provider discarded the response it was streaming, and the run
asks for it again. What was sent of it cannot be taken back; the
retried response starts new messages (#1670). A
[`Self::ProviderRetry`] saying why follows.

The turn asks the provider again, and why. Says what the turn is
doing until its next event; a stream reset sends
[`Self::ResponseDiscarded`] first.

retry_after_ms.description: How long the provider said to wait before the next request.

anyOf.description:
A titled card the session shows outside the conversation, such as a
background result.

markdown.description: The body, for clients that render markdown.

plain.description: The same body as plain text, for clients that show text as is.

anyOf.description: Something to tell the user that is not part of the conversation.

The turn waits for a person to answer `request` with
[`super::SESSION_ANSWER`] (#1660).

Input request `id` closed: a client answered it, the turn withdrew
it, or it timed out. Clients that show it stop.

Input request `id`'s timeout stopped: a client held it with
[`super::SESSION_HOLD`], so it waits for an answer.
Turn `turn` ended, and how (#1669).

The session's options changed, as after [`super::SESSION_CONFIGURE`]
or a plan approval's mode switch: all of them, replacing the last.

The provider already took steer `id` mid-request: it can no longer
be withdrawn ([`super::SESSION_UNSTEER`]), and still applies, as a
[`Self::UserMessage`] carrying `id`, at the turn's next model request.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

SessionEvent.description: One thing that happened in a session.

seq.description:
Rises by one per live event. A reset's transcript events carry 0,
except the last, which carries the seq the turn in progress began
after. So the highest seq a client has seen since its attach
response, once above 0, is always a cursor it can resume from: one
that detaches partway through a transcript resets again.

SessionGoal.description: A goal the loaded session keeps working on, independently of clients.

evaluated_turns.description: Evaluations completed, not provider calls or SDK steps.

human_steps.description: Remaining human-only work; empty while active.

last_reason.description: Why the last evaluation found the goal unmet or blocked.

phase.description: Whether the goal is working or waiting for the user.

set_at.description:
Unix time, in seconds, when the goal was set. Clients count the
goal's elapsed time from it.

SessionGoalAction.description:
A goal lifecycle change, sent through `rho/session/configure`. Unlike
model settings, these actions do not queue behind a running goal.

oneOf.description: Set a nonempty condition and start working. Refused while a turn runs.

Disarm the loop immediately, cancelling evaluation or retry waits,
but not a model turn already running. Idempotent when no goal exists.

Verify a blocked goal's human steps, or continue an active goal.
Refused while a turn runs or when there is no goal.

anyOf.description: Resume or a new user prompt verifies the previously blocked steps.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

SessionGoalPhase.description: Whether the goal is working or waiting for external human-only steps.

SessionGoalStep.description: One step the evaluator found outside the session's authority or capabilities.

action.description: What the user has to do.

reason.description: Why the session cannot do it itself.

SessionGrant.description:
What the turn a request starts may do through session control, the
`sessions` tool and `rho mcp serve`: how deep the session sits among the
sessions that started it, and the most it may do to others.

The request that opens or prompts a session names it
([`super::SessionNewParams::grant`], [`super::SessionPromptParams::grant`]),
and the daemon keeps it on the session's job
([`super::JobSummary::grant`]), so it is the daemon's record, not the
caller's environment, that says what a session may do. The daemon sets
`RHO_SESSION_DEPTH` and `RHO_SESSION_SCOPE` in the session's environment
from it, replacing any the client's environment carries.

It bounds session control, not the session: the depth stops a runaway
recursion and the scope keeps a caller's limits on the sessions it
starts. Neither is a sandbox for a session that can run commands.

Unknown fields are refused: a newer client's narrowing field must fail at
an older daemon rather than be dropped and record a wider grant.

depth.description:
How many sessions started one another to reach this one: 0 for a
session a person drives, 1 for one that session's agent started.

SessionHoldResponse.description:
Result of [`SESSION_HOLD`]: the request no longer times out, and every
attached client saw [`super::SessionEvent::InputHeld`]. Holding a
request that has no timeout, or one already held, changes nothing. A
request that closed is [`crate::ErrorCode::InputNotOpen`].

SessionId.description:
A session's id, the one `rho sessions` and `/resume` show. Opaque to
clients: send back the string the daemon gave.

report.description:
The report as rho's own frontends show it. Presentation data, not a
machine-readable contract: its shape follows the rho version.

cursor.description:
The [`SessionListResponse::next_cursor`] of the page before; absent
for the first page. A cursor the daemon did not issue is refused as
[`crate::ErrorCode::InvalidParams`].

cwd.description:
Only the sessions saved in this workspace, an absolute path,
resolved through symlinks as [`super::SESSION_NEW`] resolves its
`cwd`; absent lists every workspace's. A path that does not resolve
to a directory lists none.

limit.description:
The most sessions the page holds: 100 when absent, and at most the
daemon's limit, 1000, which the error refusing a larger one names.

SessionListResponse.description:
Result of [`SESSION_LIST`]. Following `next_cursor` never lists a session
twice, nor skips one when others are deleted between pages; a session
saved during the walk moves ahead of the cursor and is missed, so list
again from the first page for a fresh view.

next_cursor.description: The cursor of the next page; absent on the last.

SessionMcpInventory.description: Result of [`SESSION_MCP`]: a point-in-time inventory, not a subscription.

config_path.description: The configuration file the session was opened with, not the client's.

mode.description: Why the session did or did not load native MCP servers.

servers.description: Configured servers in inventory order, including disabled and failed ones.

anyOf.description: The session hosts native MCP servers.
The session's agent runtime does not host native MCP tools.
The session was opened without tools.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

SessionMcpMode.description: How a session treated its MCP configuration.

session.description: The loaded session whose servers to inspect.

SessionMcpServer.description: One configured MCP server and its session-owned status.

detail.description:
Human-readable transport, errors, exported tools, live changes, prompts
and resources. Presentation only: clients must not parse this text.

enabled.description: Whether the session enabled this server.

identity.description: Qualified server identity, including its plugin namespace when present.

status.description: Startup status; subsequent reachability changes are described in `detail`.

tool_count.description: Number of tools exported to this session's model.

anyOf.description: Connected at startup; see the server's detail for live reachability.
Startup has not finished.
Disabled by configuration.
Invalid server configuration.
Startup failed.
Startup exceeded its configured budget.
Configured but not loaded by this session.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

SessionMcpStatus.description: A server's startup outcome in a session.

agent.description:
The agent the session runs as, by id, one of the workspace's as
`rho --agent` finds them; absent, the default agent. One the
workspace does not define, or that cannot run as a session's own
agent, is [`crate::ErrorCode::SessionOpenFailed`]. A session reopened
later runs as the agent it was saved as.

cwd.description:
The session's workspace, an absolute path to an existing directory.
The daemon reads config and agents for it as `rho` started there
would.

environment.description:
The client's environment, which the session's processes run with
until a prompt brings another.

grant.description:
What the session may do through session control until a prompt
brings another grant; absent, what `environment` carries
(`RHO_SESSION_DEPTH`, `RHO_SESSION_SCOPE`), which is no limit when
it carries none. With a `parent` whose session a job of the daemon
writes, the session opens with no more than a session that job's
turn starts may have: at least one level deeper than its grant,
with no access or workspace it lacks. A session that opens with a
limit keeps it as its job's [`super::JobSummary::grant_limit`].

parent.description:
The session whose turn starts this one, such as the session of an
agent that starts a peer through session control (#1714). The daemon
records the job writing that session as the new session's job's
[`super::JobSummary::parent`], and the new session's turns then wait
for capacity in the daemon-wide agent budget, as subagent runs do
([`super::JobState::Queued`]). A session no job of the daemon writes,
such as one an in-process rho runs, records no parent, but the new
session's turns still share the budget.

setup.description: The client's choices for the session.

SessionNewResponse.description:
Result of [`SESSION_NEW`]: the session is loaded and its job is
[`crate::JobState::Idle`]. `rho sessions` lists the session once its
first prompt is saved; [`super::JOB_LIST`] shows its job.

options.description:
The session's settings and the choices it offers, which
[`super::SESSION_CONFIGURE`] changes.

SessionObserveParams.description:
Params of [`SESSION_OBSERVE`]. A session the daemon has loaded is
attached as [`SESSION_ATTACH`] attaches it. A saved session it has not
loaded stays unloaded: the daemon replays it as its file keeps it, with
how its last turn ended, then detaches the client as
[`DetachReason::NotLoaded`]. Observing starts nothing of the session, no
MCP server, OpenAPI source, or hook, and so carries no environment or
setup. With no MCP server connected, such a replay titles the session's
MCP tool calls by their names alone.

after.description:
The last event this client has, to resume after it, as for
[`SESSION_ATTACH`]. A session observed unloaded always resets.

SessionOptions.description: What a session runs with now, and what a client may change it to.

added_dirs.description: The directories the session's tools reach besides its workspace.

commands.description: The commands a prompt may start with or mention, in menu order.

fast_mode.description: Absent when the current model has no fast mode.

goal.description:
The daemon-owned goal, absent after completion, clear, or cancel.
Kept while the session is loaded, not across daemon restarts.

reasoning.description: Absent when the current model has no reasoning to configure.

SessionPart.description: A part of a session a client can leave out.

oneOf.description: The tools: the model is offered none, as with `--no-tools`.

Rho's system prompt, with the workspace's `AGENTS.md` and skills, as
with `--no-system-prompt`.
The tools that start subagents, as with `--no-subagents`.

Questions to the user: the session has no questionnaire tool, and an
MCP server's question is declined, for a client that cannot show
[`crate::Ask::Question`]. It only shapes what the session offers its
model: which connections may answer a request is decided by the
[`crate::ClientCapability::Answer`] each declared, not by this.

The session's file, as with `--no-save`: the session lives in the
daemon's memory alone. The daemon keeps it while a client follows it
or it has work under way, and discards it once it sits idle, as it
does a session that took no prompt; a daemon restart loses it. Only
a new session takes this: reopening a saved one without its file is
[`crate::ErrorCode::InvalidParams`].

content.description:
The user message: at least one block, or the prompt is refused as
[`crate::ErrorCode::InvalidParams`], as is one with an image whose
data is not a base64 PNG, JPEG, GIF, or WebP of the declared type
within the daemon's image limit. Text and images reach the model as
written. A resource reaches it as its text, and a resource link as
its description, else its name, each fenced under its URI (#1670). A
slash command the message starts with that the session runs, such as
`/init`, a prompt template, or an MCP prompt, is expanded first, as
`rho run` expands it.

environment.description:
The prompting client's environment, which the processes this turn
starts run with, and those of later turns until another prompt
brings another. Processes already running keep theirs. One whose
project trust is not the session's is refused as
[`crate::ErrorCode::ProjectTrustMismatch`].

grant.description:
What this turn, and later turns until another prompt, may do
through session control; absent, what `environment` carries, as for
[`SessionNewParams::grant`]. The daemon records it on the session's
job when the turn starts, held to the job's
[`super::JobSummary::grant_limit`]: a prompt that asks for more than
the limit is not refused, its turn runs under the limit.

idempotency_key.description:
The client's name for this prompt, which makes sending it again
safe, as after a connection that closed before the answer came. A
prompt whose key is that of the session's latest turn starts none:
it answers as the first one does, with that turn's id once the turn
began, even after the turn ended or the daemon restarted. The daemon
compares only the key, never the content. It keeps the latest turn's
key alone, so a prompt is safe to send again until another turn
starts on the session. A turn that ended before it began ran
nothing and frees its key: sending the prompt again starts a turn.
An empty key is [`crate::ErrorCode::InvalidParams`].

timeout_ms.description:
How long the turn may run, in milliseconds from when the daemon
takes the prompt. A turn still running then is cancelled and ends
[`crate::TurnOutcome::TimedOut`]. `None` sets no limit.

SessionPromptResponse.description:
Result of [`SESSION_PROMPT`]: the turn began: it saved its prompt, or,
for `/compact`, its compaction started; or, for a session another job
started ([`SessionNewParams::parent`]), it queued for capacity in the
daemon-wide agent budget. The turn runs on in the daemon;
[`super::JOB_LIST`] reports how it ends.

A turn that ends before it began answers with an error
instead: [`crate::ErrorCode::TurnEnded`], whose `data` is the turn's
[`crate::TurnOutcome`], or [`crate::ErrorCode::DaemonStopping`] when the
daemon stopped it.

turn.description:
The turn the prompt started, or, for a prompt sent again with its
[`SessionPromptParams::idempotency_key`], the turn it started the
first time. The turn's [`SessionEvent::State`]s and its
[`SessionEvent::TurnEnded`] carry it.

title.description:
The new title, surrounding whitespace trimmed. One that is empty,
holds a control character such as a newline, or runs over the
daemon's 500 characters is refused as
[`crate::ErrorCode::InvalidParams`], naming why.

SessionRenameResponse.description:
Result of [`SESSION_RENAME`]: the title is saved, and clients attached
to the session receive it as [`super::SessionEvent::TitleChanged`]. A
generated title never replaces it.

SessionReport.description: A report [`SESSION_INSPECT`] reads. Protocol minors may add reports.

oneOf.description:
What fills the model's context window on the next request, by
source.

The session's hooks, read again from their files, and their recent
activity.

The session's compaction settings as token counts, what its
compactions removed, and what the latest one did and cost.

SessionSetup.description:
Choices a client makes for a session the daemon opens for it.

The session owns its directories and the parts it leaves out but
questions: it saves them, and a reopen adds the opening request's to the
saved ones, so a later client can narrow a session, never widen it. The
opening client owns its MCP servers, whether it shows questions, and
whether its host runs the session's children: a reopened session has
those its opening request names, and none when a prompt reopens it.

That holds across the daemon's reopens. A host that opens the session
file in its own process does not keep it yet: `rho acp`'s
`session/load` and `session/resume` save the session with that
process's own flags and directories, and the terminal UI keeps what a
session saved but does not save its own `--no-*` flags.

additional_directories.description:
Directories outside the workspace the session's tools may use, as
`--add-dir` adds them: absolute paths to existing directories. An
entry that is not one is [`crate::ErrorCode::InvalidParams`], naming
it, and the session does not open. One the workspace or another
entry already holds is folded in. The session saves them; a reopen
keeps the saved ones that still exist and adds these.

child_threads.description:
Who runs the children the session's `agent` tool starts: the daemon,
when absent, or the client's host. Like the MCP servers that host
threads go through, it is the opening client's and never saved.

idle_wake.description:
What the daemon does when the session's background work finishes
while no turn runs: nothing, when absent, or a turn of its own. Like
[`Self::child_threads`], it is the opening client's and never saved.

mcp_servers.description:
MCP servers the client provides, which the session connects next to
those in config; one replaces a config server of the same name. An
entry the daemon cannot connect safely, such as plain HTTP to a host
other than this machine, is not connected, yet still replaces the
config server of its name. When a name repeats, the last entry wins.
These servers may not sample the user's model. The session does not
save them, since their `env` and `headers` may hold secrets.

sign_in.description:
Whether the session may open before its model's auth profile has
usable credentials: not, when absent, so the open fails with
[`crate::ErrorCode::SignInRequired`], or signed out. Like
[`Self::child_threads`], it is the opening client's and never saved.

without.description:
Parts of the session left out, as `rho`'s `--no-tools`,
`--no-system-prompt`, and `--no-subagents` leave them out, and
questions a client cannot show. The session saves all but
[`SessionPart::Questions`] and [`SessionPart::Saving`]; a reopen
leaves out the saved parts and these, except
[`SessionPart::Saving`], which only a new session takes.

text.description: Input for the running turn's next model request.

SessionSteerResponse.description:
Result of [`SESSION_STEER`]: the running turn accepted the input, which
applies at the turn's next model request as a
[`SessionEvent::UserMessage`] carrying `id`. A turn that ends first drops
it: a client that never saw it apply can offer it again.

No model request taking input is [`crate::ErrorCode::NotSteerable`], as
is a turn that ended before it accepted the input.

SessionSummary.description:
One session, as [`SESSION_LIST`] reports it. Only sessions with a saved
prompt whose workspace still exists are listed, and not those a program
ran: `rho run`'s, subagents', and workflow nodes'.

added_dirs.description:
The directories the session added beside its workspace, as last
saved, those since removed left out.

cwd.description:
The workspace the session was saved in, which an attach reopens it
in.

first_user_message.description:
The session's first user message on one line, cut to 80 characters,
which an untitled session is labelled with.

last_user_message.description: The session's last user message, cut like `first_user_message`.

title.description: The session's title; absent until it has one.

updated_at.description: Unix time, in seconds, of the session's last save.

id.description: The steer to withdraw, as [`SESSION_STEER`] answered it.

SessionUnsteerResponse.description:
Result of [`SESSION_UNSTEER`]. With no model request taking input, it
answers [`crate::ErrorCode::NotSteerable`] instead.

oneOf.description: Write `value`, which the setting's [`SettingKind`] takes.
Remove the setting from the file, so its default applies.

SettingEntry.description: A setting's value and where it comes from.

value.description: Absent for an optional setting that is unset.

SettingKey.description:
A setting's dotted name, which is also where `config.toml` keeps it:
`behavior.permission_mode` is the `permission_mode` key of the
`[behavior]` table.

anyOf.description: One of `choices`, by [`SettingChoice::value`].

A whole number from `min` to `max`, inclusive; no `max` means no
upper bound.
A model on one of `runtimes`.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

SettingSpec.description: One setting, as a settings screen shows it.

category.description: The id of the category whose page lists the setting.

default.description:
Absent for an optional setting that is unset by default, such as a
timeout that is off until set.

help.description:
What the setting does, without when it applies: [`Self::applies`]
says that.

overridable_per_project.description:
Whether a project may override the setting once project config
exists; settings that size the daemon itself never may.

section.description: A heading within the category page, when the page groups its rows.

SettingValue.description:
A setting's value; which variant a setting takes follows its
[`SettingKind`]: a choice is [`Self::Text`].

SignIn.description:
When a session's model needs credentials. The daemon reads it, so it has
no `Unknown`.

oneOf.description: To open: a session without them does not open.

From its first turn: a session without them opens signed out, as the
terminal UI starts, and its turns fail on the missing credentials
until a sign-in.

SteerId.description:
Identifies one accepted steer ([`super::SESSION_STEER`]): the
[`SessionEvent::UserMessage`] it applies as and its
[`SessionEvent::SteeringDelivered`] carry it, and
[`super::SESSION_UNSTEER`] withdraws the steer by it.

StopResponse.description:
Result of [`DAEMON_STOP`]: the daemon has begun shutting down. It finishes
in-flight responses, closes connections, interrupts running turns, and
exits.

anyOf.description:
Nothing did, so the daemon uses the OS store. A client signing in
should ask its user to choose one, which [`AUTH_CHOOSE_STORE`] saves.
`behavior.credential_store` in the daemon's config.

`RHO_CREDENTIAL_STORE` in the daemon's environment, which wins over
the config, so [`AUTH_CHOOSE_STORE`] refuses.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

StoreSelectedBy.description: What chose the daemon's credential store. Protocol minors may add values.

StreamId.description:
One loaded session's event stream. A new daemon, or a reload, starts
a new stream.

ToolBody.description:
Optional expandable body content.

Every variant except [`Self::Diff`] carries plain text lines; [`Self::Code`]
and [`Self::Search`] add the metadata renderers need to highlight them.

Closed: its variants carry their content under `lines`, which serde
cannot read into a unit `Unknown`, so a new variant is a protocol major.

oneOf.description:
Source code highlighted as `language`, a syntax name or file
extension such as `python` or `rs`.

Search result previews with the query that produced them, so
renderers can highlight matches with the search tool's semantics.

literal.description: The pattern is a literal substring rather than a regex.

oneOf.description: Compact diff body with per-row line numbers and change kinds.

ToolCallId.description:
Identifies one tool call; every [`ToolCallUpdate`] with the same id
updates that call.

ToolCallUpdate.description:
Opens a tool call, or updates the one with the same `id`. Absent fields
are unchanged.

content.description: Replaces the call's content when present.

display.description:
The call's card as Rho's TUI draws it; replaces the call's display
when present. While the call runs it is a
[`Presentation::Card`](crate::display::Presentation::Card) that each
start and progress update replaces; a finished call's is its final
presentation, which may be a summary card or a notification. A call
that closes `failed` without one was cut off: clients show its last
card as interrupted. Images the call produced stay in `content`.

raw_input.description: The tool's input, as the model wrote it.

ToolCard.description: Structured tool presentation for Call + Children rendering.

anyOf.description: Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

ToolCardStatus.description: Lifecycle status for the card's marker.

anyOf.description:
A file change; `old_text` is absent for a new file. A deleted file
has `deleted` set and an empty `new_text`, which an emptied file
also has.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

ToolContent.description: One piece of what a tool call shows.

anyOf.description:
Shell timeout budget in seconds; `None` when the call has no timeout.
Structured so hosts can decorate it live (elapsed clock) without
parsing display text.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

ToolFact.description: Structured child fact under a tool header.

anyOf.description: Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

ToolFamily.description: Tool-family identity, which picks the header verb's color.

anyOf.description: `verb(primary)` or bare `verb`.
Shell prompt dialect: `$ command` / `PS command`.
Agent-style `identity  detail`.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

ToolHeader.description: Header layout dialect within the shared Call + Children grammar.

anyOf.description: Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

ToolKind.description: What a tool does, so a client can pick an icon or a layout.

anyOf.description: Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

message.description:
What went wrong, for a person. An authentication failure names only
the provider and auth and how to log in, never the provider's own
text, which may echo credentials.

anyOf.description: The provider rejected the credentials, or there were none.
The provider failed the request.
A tool's host failed, not just one tool call.

The session's config cannot run, such as a model the provider does
not offer.
Anything else.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

TurnErrorKind.description: What kind of failure ended a turn.

TurnId.description:
Identifies one turn of a session: what a prompt starts, from the
job leaving rest until it rests again. [`super::SESSION_PROMPT`]
answers with it, and [`SessionEvent::State`],
[`SessionEvent::TurnEnded`], and
[`super::SessionAttachResponse::turn`] carry it, so a client tells
its own turn from another client's by id. The daemon keeps a
session's last turn's id with the session's job, so it names the
same turn after a restart.

anyOf.description:
The model gave its final answer. `text` is the answer whole, as the
turn saved it, which a client that missed chunks or saw a provider
retry restart a reply can show instead of what it gathered.

The turn used its model-step limit before the model answered; `text`
is the reply text of its last step, possibly empty.
A client cancelled it.

The daemon cancelled it at the time limit its prompt set,
[`super::SessionPromptParams::timeout_ms`], repeated here.
It failed.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

UncheckedKey.description: Why [`AUTH_KEY`] saved a key the provider did not check.

message.description:
The reason in words, for a person: what went wrong when the provider
could not be reached, such as `HTTP 404`. It never contains the key.

reason.description: Why, for a program to branch on.

anyOf.description: Rho lists no models for the provider, so it cannot ask about a key.

The provider's models endpoint did not answer the question: it could
not be reached, or it failed with a status other than a refusal, as a
gateway without `/models` does.

The provider's models endpoint answered 403 Forbidden: the key may
not list models, as a key restricted to running them may not, so
the endpoint says nothing about whether it works.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

UncheckedReason.description: Why a key went unchecked. Protocol minors may add reasons.

anyOf.description: Removed before it reached the conversation: it never applies.

The provider already took it ([`SessionEvent::SteeringDelivered`]):
it still applies.
Already in the conversation.

The running turn never accepted that id: another turn's, or one a
turn dropped when it ended.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.
Nothing sets it; the value is its default.
The user's global file sets it.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

ValueSource.description: Where a setting's value comes from.

VersionFix.description: Which side of an incompatible pair has to change.

oneOf.description:
The running daemon is older than the client. Replacing it with the
client's version lets them talk; [`VersionMismatch::restart`] says
what that costs.

The client is older than the daemon. Update the client, or restart
one that was updated while it ran.

VersionMismatch.description:
An incompatible handshake. The daemon sends this as the `data` of a
[`crate::ErrorCode::VersionMismatch`] error; its `Display` is the
actionable message for users.

Both sides must read this whatever their versions, so it only ever gains
optional fields, also while the protocol is unstable; CI holds it to
that.

restart.description:
What restarting the daemon would cost. The daemon sends it with
[`VersionFix::RestartDaemon`], so a client can say so before anyone
restarts it, and can tell a daemon nobody is using.
